q: A laptop battery is visibly swollen. What is the best next action?
options: Press it flat and continue testing
Stop using the device and follow the manufacturer’s safe battery-service procedure
Puncture it to release pressure
Run a long stress test
why: Swelling is a safety hazard. Do not compress, puncture or stress the battery. Isolate the device from use and follow qualified service guidance.

Factory-reset both devices
Verify cable data support and the phone’s USB connection mode

q: A client must resolve a hostname before opening an HTTPS page. Which service/port pairing normally identifies the DNS query service?
options: DNS on UDP/TCP port 53
HTTPS on TCP port 443
SSH on TCP port 22
SMTP on TCP port 25
why: DNS uses port 53, commonly UDP for ordinary queries and TCP where needed. HTTPS on port 443 protects the subsequent web connection; it is not the name-resolution service.

options: The display refresh rate

The local print queue

q: A user mirrors two drives and calls this a complete backup. Which incident still threatens both current copies?
options: One mirrored drive failing while the other remains healthy
A data read from either drive
An accidental file deletion replicated across the mirror
A temporary loss of the monitor signal
why: Mirroring primarily supports availability after certain hardware failures. Deletions and other logical changes can affect both copies, so a separate recoverable backup is still needed.

q: A lab VM snapshot exists only on the same physical disk as the VM. What does the snapshot NOT protect against?

q: On a systemd-based Linux lab machine, which read-only command can inspect journal logs, subject to the current account’s permissions?
options: journalctl
rm -rf /var/log
chmod -R 777 /
mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda
why: journalctl views the systemd journal without formatting or deleting data. Some entries require authorized access; request only the needed privilege rather than weakening permissions or running unrelated destructive commands.
